description: DuckDB tests that cannot pass by design: the SlateDB test configs run every test inside an attached duckdb_objfs:// catalog instead of DuckDB's default database, and the extension's own tests expect to configure the filesystem themselves. These fail the same way when the attached catalog is a plain local DuckDB file.

skip_tests.reason: Tests run in the attached catalog '__test__config__slatedb', but these tests expect the default catalog to be named 'memory' (CURRENT_CATALOG, SHOW ALL TABLES, DESCRIBE), reference memory.* or memory.temp explicitly, COPY FROM DATABASE memory, or expect 'main' as the current schema and search path.
The test's default database stays attached next to '__test__config__slatedb', so SHOW DATABASES/SCHEMAS, duckdb_databases(), pragma_database_list and pragma_database_size() return an extra database.
The attached database uses DuckDB's default persistent storage version (v1.0.0), which rejects VARIANT columns and does not keep GEOMETRY statistics; the tests assume the in-memory default database.
PRAGMA checkpoint_abort is aimed at the default database, but the aborted checkpoint invalidates '__test__config__slatedb', which every later statement uses.
The test sets a 1 MiB memory_limit, which the additional attached database exhausts.

Extension tests that set up duckdb_objfs themselves: they expect an uninitialized filesystem, attach the mapped database explicitly, or rely on data surviving a restart (which the memory backend does not provide). They run under 'make test' without the SlateDB test config.
